subject: Assessment approach & owners for BrightLane validation
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-21T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Assessment approach & owners for BrightLane validation

Hi Amit —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and a proposed path forward so we can lock timelines and owners. TL;DR: we recommend a two-track validation with a short offline benchmark + an optional 2-week live shadow. Either path can be used to sign off on the pilot depending on how much production traffic you want to route.

Discovery recap (short):
- Primary goal: reduce triage time for claims review and surface high-confidence suggestions for reviewers.
- Key constraints: PHI handling & de-identification required, sub-second target latency in reviewer UI, and <1% unacceptable hallucination rate on high-risk categories.

Proposed validation tracks (pick one or run both):
1) Offline benchmark (recommended initial step)
   - What: run Redwood models on a withheld, de-identified dataset and score outputs against human labels.
   - Benefits: quick, reproducible, safe (no live traffic), and lets us iterate on prompts/quantization before shadowing.
   - Typical data needs: 1k–2k labeled examples per vertical/intent (we can be flexible).

2) Live shadow (online)
   - What: mirror a sample of production traffic to Redwood inference with no impact to end users; collect model outputs for live scoring and reviewer A/B comparisons.
   - Benefits: real-world behavior, latency measurement, and UI regression checks.

Success criteria / rubric (proposal):
- Accuracy (Top-1 exact match vs label) >= 78% on core intents
- Hallucination rate (policy-safe flagging) < 1% on high-risk categories
- Latency P95 (end-to-end inference) < 400ms for median payloads
- Reviewer accept rate uplift >= 12% vs baseline in shadow
- Cost estimate: USD per 1k tokens (we'll provide exact once we see length distribution)

Ownership & roles:
- Sales lead / commercial: Jordan Blake (me) — contract, commercial cadence
- Technical lead / evaluation: Karthik Iyer — offline scripts, rubric, ingestion
- Trial operations / CS: Marissa Cole — shadow ops, reviewer workflows, acceptance testing

Deliverables & timeline (proposed):
- Week 0 (this week): sign off on approach & dataset access details
- Week 1: receive de-identified sample + Redwood runs offline benchmark (2–4 business days)
- Week 2: review rubric results, iterate prompts/configs
- Week 3–4 (optional): 2-week live shadow with weekly checkpoints
- Week 5: final acceptance report + recommendation for production rollout

Attachments I've included: assessment_rubric_v1.xlsx (rubric + scoring thresholds), shadow_playbook_v2.pdf (ops checklist), mutual_action_plan_BrightLane_20261025.docx (mutual action plan draft).

Decision items for BrightLane:
- Confirm which track you want to run (offline only vs offline + shadow)
- Confirm dataset owner & ETA for sample (de-identified)
- Confirm preferred kickoff date (we're proposing Oct 28 or Oct 29)

If you're okay, I'll loop in our security contact (we've copied karthik who will connect to your security team) and Marissa will build the trial calendar.

Cheers,

Jordan Blake

Hi Amit —

Quick answers from the technical side:
1) Offline sample size guidance: 1k labeled examples per vertical gives reasonable confidence for initial tuning; 2k per vertical is preferred if you have the labels. We'll provide bootstrap confidence intervals in the report.

2) PHI & data handling options:
   - Option A (preferred for speed): de-identified extracts (BrightLane does de-id) and you provide S3 link with restricted credentials. We run inference in our isolated infra and produce aggregate reports only.
   - Option B (VPC/on-prem): we can deploy our private inference package inside your VPC (security review required). Effort: typically 2–3 weeks for access plus connectivity checks.

3) Live shadow config: mirror 5–10% of traffic to start (sample stratified by vertical). We do not persist raw payloads in plaintext logs and can disable telemetry. We'll sign an appendix for logging retention and show you config that redacts tokens.

Evaluation rubric (high level; details in attached assessment_rubric_v1.xlsx):
- Metrics we will compute: Exact-match accuracy, top-3 containment, hallucination flags (policy/medical hallucination classifier), latency distribution, reviewer accept-rate uplift, and per-request token cost.
- Acceptance thresholds: we recommend setting conservative gating for the first rollout (accuracy >= 78%, hallucination < 1%). These are negotiable based on your risk tolerance.

Operational notes: we'll ship a simple runner (Python) that takes a CSV (id, prompt, expected_label) and emits per-example scores + aggregate report. We can run it ourselves or share the runner for you to execute in your environment.

I've attached the current rubric and a short "shadow playbook" that covers telemetry and reviewer sync points.
